name: Spektre Labs
tagline: What you say should equal what you do. We measure the gap.
subtext: Independent research lab in Helsinki. One idea: coherence you can measure — what a system declares should equal what it does. Proven in the Spektre Corpus, shipping as σ-gate.
author: Lauri Elias Rainio

about.description: Spektre Labs is an independent research laboratory based in Helsinki.
overview: Spektre Labs is an independent research laboratory based in Helsinki.

The lab is dedicated to the discovery of structural invariants across complex systems. Its work focuses on identifying patterns that persist across domains and scales, from physical systems to cognition, artificial intelligence, and institutional dynamics.
Everything published is open. The papers live in the Spektre Corpus; the working proof is σ-gate — a free, zero-dependency tool that enforces the same rule in AI output.

researchOutput.title: Research Output
paragraphs: The primary artifact produced by Spektre Labs is the Spektre Corpus, a collection of formal research papers investigating coherence, feedback failure, and collapse dynamics across multiple theoretical frameworks.
The corpus examines how structural relationships emerge across domains including physics, information theory, dynamical systems, and institutional systems.
All research artifacts are published openly.

authorSection.title: Author
authorSection.name: Lauri Elias Rainio
authorSection.bio: Lauri Elias Rainio is an independent systems architect and self-taught researcher. His work begins from a single question — what makes any system, whether code, a market, an institution, or a mind, hold its structure or collapse — and pursues it across software, formal theory, and design. He arrived at research the way he learned everything else: directly and obsessively, from first principles, building the engineering, machine learning, and formal methods behind the Spektre protocol himself. Spektre Labs is the consolidation of that work — one invariant, 1 = 1, traced from physics to cognition and made executable in code.

hero.headline: Does it do what it says?
hero.axiomGloss: What a system promises should match what it delivers. σ is the distance between the two.
hero.tagline: What you say should equal what you do. We measure the gap.
hero.sub: Spektre Labs studies why systems hold together — and why they break. We turned that study into running code: σ-gate, a free tool that checks whether an AI's output is safe and honest before it ships.
description: Spektre Labs studies why systems hold together — and why they break.
We turned that study into running code: tools that check whether an AI's output is actually safe and honest before it ships.

whatWeDo.title: What we do
whatWeDo.description: We study one thing in many places: what keeps a system — code, a market, a mind, an institution — holding together, and what makes it fall apart. Then we build tools that measure it.
whatWeDo.detail: Research focuses on invariants governing coherence, feedback dynamics, and systemic collapse.

research.title: Research
research.description: Spektre Labs investigates structural invariants across complex systems through several interconnected research layers.
research.detail: These include theoretical foundations, complex systems, artificial intelligence, cognition, information architectures, and physics.

method.title: Method
method.description: Research is conducted through computational orchestration: a methodology combining formal modeling, computational exploration, and iterative falsification to identify structural invariants across domains.

method.title: Computational Orchestration
method.description: Spektre Labs conducts research through computational orchestration, a methodology that uses computational systems to explore, test, and formalize structural hypotheses about complex systems.
introduction: Spektre Labs conducts research through computational orchestration, a methodology that uses computational systems to explore, test, and formalize structural hypotheses about complex systems.

The objective is not to model isolated phenomena, but to identify structural invariants that persist across domains, from physical and informational systems to cognition, artificial intelligence, and institutional dynamics.

Computation serves as an exploratory instrument, enabling systematic traversal of large theoretical spaces and revealing structures that may not emerge through conventional analytical reasoning alone.

steps.title: Formal Modeling
paragraphs: Structural hypotheses are expressed in mathematical or algorithmic form, defining variables, constraints, and transformation rules. The aim is to produce a structure that can be examined across multiple domains.

steps.title: Computational Exploration
paragraphs: Computational systems explore the implications of candidate structures, enabling rapid traversal of theoretical search spaces and revealing emergent patterns.

steps.title: Iterative Falsification
paragraphs: Candidate structures are repeatedly stress-tested. Unstable formulations are discarded, while coherent structures that survive falsification are retained.

steps.title: Structural Synthesis
paragraphs: Surviving structures are integrated into broader theoretical frameworks, allowing cross-domain correspondences and deeper invariants to emerge.

crossDomainValidation.title: Cross-Domain Validation
paragraphs: Structures identified in one domain are examined across others, including complex systems, information architectures, cognition, artificial intelligence, institutional systems, and cosmology.
When a structural relationship appears consistently across independent domains, it suggests the presence of a deeper invariant.

roleOfComputationalSystems.title: Role of Computational Systems
paragraphs: Computational systems assist with exploration, verification, and falsification across large conceptual spaces.
They function as amplifiers of reasoning, while the human researcher directs the research program and evaluates resulting structures.

researchPhilosophy.title: Research Philosophy
paragraphs: Spektre Labs focuses on structural discovery: identifying invariant relationships that govern coherence, stability, and collapse across complex systems.
